title: Allele frequency

blocks.what_we_do: We keep variants with a minor allele frequency of at least 1%. We use this rule for the main array scan.
blocks.why:
The minor allele frequency (MAF) is how often the less common allele appears in the samples we analyse. For example, if one allele is found in 3 of 100 copies, the MAF is 3%.

A rare allele gives very few samples in some genotype groups. The ordinary [logistic regression](docs/glossary.md#logistic-regression), the test we use later for association, is then unstable. A 1% filter is a choice made for this course. It does not define what is biologically important.

Frequencies depend on [ancestry](docs/glossary.md#ancestry), which is the geographic origin of a person's ancestors. They also depend on how the samples were selected. They depend on how PLINK counts chromosome copies too. For example, men have one X chromosome and women have two.
blocks.you_need: The dataset from step 4.2, which we call state 4.2.
blocks.command:
```{r s4-3}
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "4.2"), "--maf", "0.01", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "4.3")))
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "4.3", "4.2")
guided_register(cfg, "4.3", "4.2", 1844, 239019, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s4-2_state --maf 0.01 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s4-3_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--maf 0.01` removes variants with a minor allele frequency below 1%, and PLINK counts chromosome copies correctly for each chromosome.

`--pfile` selects the PLINK 2 input files.

`--make-pgen` writes a new copy of the data in PLINK 2 format.

`--out` sets the start of the names of the new files.

`--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads.

`--memory 2048` sets the memory PLINK may use, in MiB.
blocks.expected_result:
56,420 variants are removed because of their observed frequencies. 239,019 variants remain. The simulation did not plant a special list of rare artefacts (errors caused by the technology).

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the error message, and check the previous step. Keep your command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: It finds sparse variants, which carry little information in this sample. It does not tell you whether a rare allele is real. It also does not tell you whether the variant could be analysed in a larger study.
blocks.quick_check:
Can the minor and major label of an allele change between populations?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. The label describes how common the allele is in the sample. It is not a fixed property of the allele.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s4-3_state.*` and the list of excluded variants that lets the course repeat this step.
